arpeggio.hint: One note per grid slot, following the click — turn the demo on (pad or strum) and it plays the arpeggio note by note. Lock onto one position and take it through all 12 keys before moving to the next: an arpeggio drill is one shape found in 12 places.

1.title: 1 · Triads
1.description: Make the most stable chords automatic: I, IV, V, vi. The goal is changing chords without breaking the pulse.

2.title: 2 · Full diatonic
2.description: Add ii, iii and vii°, and walk all seven chords of the key.

3.title: 3 · Sevenths
3.description: Trade triads for sevenths and hear the difference between Imaj7 and V7.

4.title: 4 · Blues dominants
4.description: Twelve-bar blues and all-dominant harmony. Get used to the sound of not resolving.

5.title: 5 · Fusion / Neo-soul
5.description: Extensions, borrowed chords and secondary dominants — how out-of-key notes earn their place.

rhythm.editHint: Click a cell to cycle: rest → normal → accent → ghost. Edits sound from the next bar.
rhythm.subdivisionHint: Listen to two rounds before you strum along. Keep the hand moving up and down throughout — ghost cells still brush the strings, they just do not ring.
rhythm.grooveHint: Rhythm is the point; the chord is only a vamp. Get the accents in the right slots before you worry about tone.

quarter.title: Stage 1 — Quarter notes
quarter.description: Land exactly on the click. There is no nuance here, only in time or out of time.

eighth.title: Stage 2 — Eighths and offbeats
eighth.description: Add the offbeat. The offbeat drill removes the downbeat click on purpose — with nothing to lean on you find out how steady you really are.

sixteenth.title: Stage 3 — Sixteenths
sixteenth.description: Four slots per beat: 1 e & a. Drill the e and the a separately so the hand learns where each slot lives.

syncopation.title: Stage 4 — Dotted notes and ties
syncopation.description: Accents stop landing on whole-number positions. The dotted eighth and the tresillo are the ancestors of every syncopation you will meet.

funk.title: FUNK
funk.description: A sixteenth-note grid packed with ghost notes, and the accent back on the one. The hand never stops.

soul.title: SOUL / R&B
soul.description: Eighth-note based, accents on the 2 and 4 backbeat; all the give and take lives in the offbeats.

shuffle.title: Shuffle / Blues
shuffle.description: Triplet feel. Push swing from 50% straight to 67% full shuffle and hear every shade in between.

sixEight.description: Slow 6/8 and 12/8: the two-big-beat feel and the six-small-beat feel are two different ways of walking.

intro.what: RCS is an online practice room for guitarists: metronome, fretboard, circle of fifths, and theory notes on one screen. Open a browser tab and play — nothing to install, nothing to sign up for, and your practice records stay on your own device.
intro.why: Metronomes give you a pulse. Theory sites give you diagrams. Nobody fills the gap between them — the one where you understand the idea but your hands still don't know where to go. RCS lets you hear the beat, see where the notes are, and read why those are the notes, all at once.
intro.privacy: No ads while you practise. No ad container exists on any screen that plays a click — that is a product promise, not a setting.

highlight.rhythm: Metronome, subdivision drills, and groove sheets to play along with, including swing and accent design
highlight.chords: Numeral progressions, the 12-key cycle, circle-of-fifths navigation, and any progression you write yourself
highlight.scales: Full-fretboard note names and degrees, five position frames, and scale practice that follows the click

knowledgeIndex.title: Theory
knowledgeIndex.description: Notes on scales, chords, progressions, and rhythm — written for someone with a guitar in hand: when to use it, why that note, and what it sounds like.

legal.footerNote: Practice records stay in your browser
